secrets.title: Alien Egg
secrets.summary: There is a hidden Alien Egg in the game files that can be spawned using third-party trainers. The egg glows in the dark when spawned. The Alien Egg was eventually added to GTA Online in the Gunrunning update as supplies that the player can steal. To trigger the mission, the player must complete 600 resupply missions and start a new one between 21:00 and 23:00. If all conditions are met, the game may randomly begin...

secrets.title: Alien in the Ice
secrets.summary: In Ludendorff, North Yankton, underneath the train bridge the crew passes in the Prologue, there is a frozen creek. The player is able to drive down an embankment and onto the ice, where an alien is visible, frozen underneath it. It can also be found during the mission Bury the Hatchet.

secrets.title: Collector's Edition Black Light Map
secrets.summary: Using a black light/UV light on the blueprint map that comes with the Collector's Edition reveals markings, map legends, secrets and text. Most of the things that appear are pointing towards the existence of UFOs. Three of the collectible Spaceship Parts are also shown in the map.

secrets.title: UFOs
secrets.summary: Multiple UFOs can be seen, most of them only after 100% Completion is obtained. Three appear in the sky and one appears underwater. *One of the UFOs appears above Fort Zancudo. The words "segregate and rearrange" are written on the side. Segregate being an anagram, when rearranged, it spells out "Easter egg". On the bottom of the ship, an unknown device can be seen rotating around. From 3AM to 4AM, a spinning green...

secrets.title: Ghost of Jolene Cranley-Evans
secrets.summary: Between 23:00 and 0:00, a female ghost appears on the eastern peak of Mount Gordo. It doesn't react to any actions the player takes towards it unless they get too close, in which case the ghost will then disappear until the player backs off. During the time it is present, the word "JOCK" appears written in blood below where the ghost is floating, and a distressed female voice can occasionally be heard. In an article...

secrets.title: Bigfoot vs Beast
secrets.summary: After eating all 27 Peyote Plants, golden ones will appear; one in a different location for each day of the week. When eaten, they will turn the player into Bigfoot. If consumed in order (from Sunday to Saturday), when eating the final plant, a dead animal will be lying nearby, along with the body of the Sasquatch Hunter from The Last One. Growling will cause a howl to sound from the distance, to which the player...

secrets.title: Thermal Bigfoot
secrets.summary: In the mission Predator, Michael must use a sniper rifle fitted with a thermal scope to find the O'Neil brothers in the woods at night. If the player zooms in on the thermal heat dot in the bottom right, it appears to be the Sasquatch standing still. Shooting it does nothing and it abruptly disappears within a few seconds of being spotted.

secrets.title: The Chupacabra
secrets.summary: Chupacabra Street is named after the Chupacabra, a Latin American cryptid.

secrets.title: Angry Text/Phone Call
secrets.summary: If the player shoots a gun, launches grenades, throws molotov cocktails, or fires rockets at a protagonist's house while playing as another protagonist, they will receive an angry call or text telling them to stop. If the player sneaks around a protagonist's house as another protagonist, they will receive a text asking if they are the one sneaking around. If the player steals a protagonist's vehicle as another...

secrets.title: Amanda's stripper name
secrets.summary: Hinted by the license plate of her Sentinel, Amanda De Santa's stage name from her days as a stripper was "Krystal".

secrets.title: Beta map
secrets.summary: A beta map of Los Santos can be found inside Los Santos Transit stations and the Vanilla Unicorn's employee area.

secrets.title: Beta photos
secrets.summary: In the Yellow Jack Inn are framed photographs of Trevor Philips sitting in the cockpit of a small plane with the registration LS-5680, while the background appears to be a beta version of the Grand Senora Desert. Furthermore, LS-5680 can be seen in the Thomson Scrapyard. Several postcards can be found for sale at the Del Perro Pier and in certain clothing stores, featuring what appear to be beta photos of various...

secrets.title: Big O juice stand
secrets.summary: In both Vinewood Hills and Grapeseed, a Big O juice stand can be found with a large orange ball on top of it. Shooting or walking into the ball will cause it to detach and roll around. It has very little weight and can be moved easily.

secrets.title: Black Cellphones
secrets.summary: Dialing 1-999-367-3767 will call an unlisted contact called "Black Cellphones", after which a small explosion will occur over the player's head and their phone color will be changed to black.

secrets.title: Bodhi
secrets.summary: The Bodhi is named after Bodhi Ogg, the son of Trevor Philips' voice and motion capture actor Steven Ogg.

secrets.title: California
secrets.summary: There is a wrecked pickup truck bed in Stab City with a real-life California license plate. As seen in alpha build screenshots published by Rockstar North developers, this is left over from when California license plates were used as placeholders for the San Andreas license plates. A sign in Sandy Shores advertises a business known as "Salton Sea Real Estate". This is likely an oversight, as the Salton Sea is the...

secrets.title: CNT Billboards
secrets.summary: Along Elgin Avenue in Vinewood Hills is a CNT billboard made to look like a TV, with its "screen" being breakable glass. It is possible to both launch vehicles and skydive through it. A nearly identical billboard can be found near the Los Santos International Airport; however, the glass on this one cannot be broken.

secrets.title: Confederate Battle Flag
secrets.summary: A Confederate battle flag used to be hung at Braddock Farm and The Range. The latter's was replaced with an American flag in the enhanced edition, while the former's was covered by a sign reading, "Trespassers will be shot! Survivors will be shot again!" in 2017, at the same time as GTA Onlines Doomsday Heist update. If the sign is somehow removed, the battle flag can still be seen underneath.

secrets.title: Face on Mount Chiliad
secrets.summary: On the Xbox 360 and PS3 versions, the face of Rockstar Leeds artist David Dixon (internally named with his initials "dd_signature") could be seen on the side of Mount Chiliad. In the enhanced editions, this face was replaced with a drawing of a rooster shaped to look like a penis.

secrets.title: Graffiti defacement/messages
secrets.summary: Various instances of defacing graffiti and messages can be found around the map, some of which only appear as the story progresses. Along Interstate 2 in Downtown Los Santos is graffiti featuring the text "This is broken - Can I return it?" and a drawing of the American flag. This exact same text and drawing can also be seen on a banner along the train tracks in Rancho. On a wall of the Vespucci Beach Recreation...

secrets.title: Greentooth
secrets.summary: At the north end of the Mount Chiliad train tunnel, a green smiley face with sharp teeth - known as Greentooth - can be seen spraypainted on the wall. This is an inside joke between videogame developers.

secrets.title: Hot Wheels
secrets.summary: The name of the auto service business Ruedas De Fuego translates to "Fire Wheels" in English. This is possibly a reference to the Hot Wheels toy car brand.

secrets.title: Hunting Pictures
secrets.summary: During the Hunting side-activity, Trevor is instructed by Cletus Ewing to send him photographs of the animals he shoots. It is possible, however, to send them to other contacts instead. Their responses range from simply commenting on the picture, to utter confusion or disgust. Certain contacts have specific responses while others share randomized, generic ones. It is also possible to send Cletus a photograph of a...

secrets.title: HVYMTL
secrets.summary: Combining the names of HVY and MTL - two heavy-duty vehicle manufacturers - spells out HVYMTL, a disemvoweling of "heavy metal".

secrets.title: Mount Chiliad Mural
secrets.summary: A mysterious mural inside the tramway station atop Mount Chiliad includes a drawing of what appears to be a jetpack, leading to speculation that such a device might be hidden somewhere on the map, though it was later revealed that it was an unimplemented idea from the game developers. Although data files for a jetpack were present in the game, the vehicle itself was later scrapped for unknown reasons, though a...

secrets.title: Real Brands
secrets.summary: In the original versions of the game, on the Lucky Plucker menu boards, stickers for the real life beverages, Sprite, Barq's, and Fanta could be seen. These were removed in the enhanced edition.

secrets.title: Red Ring Of Death
secrets.summary: A donut advertised on the Bleeter page for Rusty Brown's Ring Donuts is called the Red Ring of Death donut. This is a reference to the infamous Xbox 360 error nicknamed the Red Ring of Death.

secrets.title: Rockstar Games/Scotland
secrets.summary: GTA V contains numerous references to Rockstar Games and Rockstar North, the developers of the Grand Theft Auto series and the games' primary development team, respectively. *Various Los Santos Department of Sanitation bins have the text "RSGEDI021277" written on the side, referencing Rockstar Games and Edinburgh, the location of Rockstar North's headquarters; while others have "RSNRTH281078", also referencing...

secrets.title: Snowman
secrets.summary: In East Los Santos, a Snowman is visible inside a room of the Fridgit warehouse, behind some boxes. The room cannot be entered, but can be seen through a gap in the door and fired into.

secrets.title: The Infinity Killer
secrets.summary: Throughout Blaine County and the Grand Senora Desert, various traces of serial killer Merle Abrahams - also known as "The Infinity Killer" due to his obsession with the number 8 and infinity - can be found. Following the clues can lead to the locations of his victims' bodies. In Sandy Shores, a newspaper clipping can be found that claims Abrahams passed away in 2004 while awaiting trial for the abduction, torture...

secrets.title: "This Does Not Exist"
secrets.summary: There is a small floating white square in the sky and small white cube far beneath the map that contain the text "this does not exist"; the latter is unable to be seen in-game without mods. These are likely developer oversights.

secrets.title: Underwater Wrecks
secrets.summary: Surrounding the map are underwater wrecks, ranging between planes, ships, military vehicles, a submarine, a decompression chamber, and even a UFO (see above). Amongst some of the wreckages, the player can find weapons, armor, health packs, and briefcases containing money.

secrets.title: Whale Skeleton
secrets.summary: A whale skeleton can be found underwater, just off of Banham Canyon.

secrets.title: Wrecked Tank
secrets.summary: A wrecked T-34 can be found at Rogers Salvage & Scrap.

secrets.title: El Burro
secrets.summary: The names of El Burro Heights and El Burro Boulevard refer to multiple notable characters named El Burro throughout the Grand Theft Auto franchise, the first being from the original .

secrets.title: Grand Theft Auto Font
secrets.summary: On a wall next to the tunnel on Low Power Street, there is graffiti of Los Santos sprayed in the style of the original Grand Theft Auto logo.

secrets.title: Ten Points!
secrets.summary: Sometimes when Trevor hits a pedestrian in a vehicle, he will shout "ten points!", referencing the scoring system in the original Grand Theft Auto.

secrets.title: Donald Love
secrets.summary: In Franklin's house in Vinewood Hills on one of the bookshelves, there is a book entitled "The Liberty King" featuring the artwork of Donald Love from Grand Theft Auto III on its cover. This Easter egg has appeared in previous GTA games.

secrets.title: Franklin's ringtone
secrets.summary: Franklin's ringtone is a low pitch sample of the song "Bump To The Music", which first appeared in Grand Theft Auto III and was created by the in-universe band Fatamarse.

secrets.title: Candy Suxxx
secrets.summary: Several references to an variant of Candy Suxxx, a porn star in GTA Vice City, appear in GTA V. The name of Tracey De Santa's online persona, Tracey Suxxx, is possibly inspired by her. A transaction to "CandySuxxx Mobile Internet" can be seen in Franklin's Maze Bank account. The name appears on a star along the Vinewood Walk of Fame. The cover of a Pussycat magazine issue claims that she was interviewed by them at...

secrets.title: BJ Smith
secrets.summary: BJ Smith, a minor character in GTA Vice City, is referenced in the name of a recreation center and park in Chamberlain Hills - the BJ Smith Recreational Center.

secrets.title: DJ Toni Billboard
secrets.summary: There is a billboard of Toni, a radio DJ from the , under the Vinewood Sports LS store in Hawick.

secrets.title: Heat Boiler Suits
secrets.summary: One of the outfits available for heists, the green boiler suit with the hockey mask, is a clear reference to the movie Heat, which was previously referenced in a similar way in the heist mission planned at the Malibu Club in GTA Vice City.

secrets.title: The Twins Painting
secrets.summary: There is an advert for The Directors Cut Hair Salon featuring the artwork of one of The Twins painted on a building.

secrets.title: Bigfoot
secrets.summary: The Sasquatch Hunter in The Last One claims he has been hunting Bigfoot for eight years, likely referencing the time between the releases of GTA V and GTA San Andreas. The latter game had a popular myth that Bigfoot was able to be found, prompting players to relentlessly search for him.

secrets.title: CJ Surveillance
secrets.summary: In Lester's House, there is a book called Surveillance on the bookshelf. A promotional screenshot of GTA San Andreas featuring CJ can be seen on the cover.

secrets.title: Cops Donuts
secrets.summary: In I Fought the Law..., Michael and Trevor, dressed as police officers on motorcycles, throw their half eaten donuts to the ground. This is likely a nod to the mission Reuniting the Families in GTA San Andreas, as during this mission, two motorcycle cops drop their donuts and begin to chase CJ, Sweet, Ryder, and Big Smoke in their car.

secrets.title: C.R.A.S.H.
secrets.summary: During the mission Eye in the Sky, the pilot that is flying with Trevor will remark that the "LSPD have come a long way concerning racism in the last two decades". The pilot may be referencing the events of GTA San Andreas and C.R.A.S.H. - which itself would also reference the Los Angeles riots in 1992.

secrets.title: Follow the Damn Train!
secrets.summary: During the mission Derailed, a gold medal objective is named "Better than CJ". This refers to the infamously difficult mission Wrong Side of the Tracks in GTA San Andreas, in which CJ needs to follow a train. Additionally, on the side of the highway near the RON Alternates Wind Farm, the numbers "1 25 8 20 4 23 6 20 4 20 3 10" are written. Each number corresponds to a letter, spelling out "A Y H T D W F T D T C J"...

secrets.title: Founding Dates
secrets.summary: The Los Santos Country Club was established in 1992, a nod to the year of the setting of GTA San Andreas The San Andreas Flight School was established in 2004, the same year GTA San Andreas was released.

secrets.title: Gold Records
secrets.summary: In Franklin's house in Vinewood Hills there are three gold records on the wall, one of which belongs to OG Loc from GTA San Andreas. There is also a Madd Dogg CD sitting on top of the DJ Booth, and a red and blue coloured artwork of Madd Dogg with MADD written across the bottom. Being media personalities, they are the only type of characters who can have variants between universes.

secrets.title: Hot Coffee Mod
secrets.summary: On Denise Clinton's Lifeinvader, she posts, "No wonder I never get a second date with that boy walking in every time I have a man home for coffee." This is likely a reference to the Hot Coffee Mod controversy. In Legal Trouble, a Weazel News headline reads, "new videogame fails to shock even most skittish politician," further referencing the controversy.

secrets.title: Sweet & Kendl
secrets.summary: During the mission Hood Safari, on the last turn before arriving in Grove Street, three Chamberlain Gangster Families members riding BMXs down Grove Street away from the cul-de-sac can be seen, with the outfit of the CGF gangster leading the group closely resembling CJ, a likely allusion towards the introductory Sweet & Kendl mission.

secrets.title: Train Date
secrets.summary: Writing on the side of trains reads "LS2004", possibly a nod to Los Santos and the year GTA San Andreas was released.

secrets.title: Vinewood Girl Dollars
secrets.summary: If the player goes into the Yellow Jack Inn in Sandy Shores, behind the counter will be several "$69" bills hanging on the wall. Pictured on these bills is the artwork of the Vinewood Girl that appeared on the disc and cover art of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. The bills also appear to have "10.12.2004 6PM" on them, 14 days before Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas was released.

secrets.title: Welcome Back
secrets.summary: In Chamberlain Hills, close to Franklin's house, there is graffiti which reads "Welcome Back - We missed you last time", welcoming players back to San Andreas.

secrets.title: Broker Clothing
secrets.summary: A brand of clothing called Broker, a reference to the borough of Broker in Liberty City from GTA IV, can be found in GTA V in the form of wearable clothing and outlet stores. The shop also features a picture of Broker's skyline on its logo.

secrets.title: Daddy's Back
secrets.summary: One of the lines Michael can say when entering his house is "Daddy's back, bitches!" This is similar to Dave Bosoy's famous line from the very beginning of GTA IV, "Daddy's back, you bitches!"

secrets.title: Dial-up Tone
secrets.summary: If the player dials 948-555-0100 in their in-game phone, the dial-up modem sound will be heard upon calling. This is the same number for ZiT in GTA IV. The same will happen if the player dials any cheat codes from GTA IV and Episodes from Liberty City.

secrets.title: Honkers Stickers
secrets.summary: At the Vanilla Unicorn, there is a sticker on the lockers in the back room for Honkers Gentlemen's Club in GTA IV. These stickers can also be seen at Tattoo Parlors around San Andreas.

secrets.title: Liberty City GPS
secrets.summary: In many of the vehicles in the original version of the game, the in-vehicle GPS shows a map of Liberty City from GTA IV. This is likely due to the texture just simply being ported over.

secrets.title: Liberty City License Plate
secrets.summary: Near the O'Neil's ranch, a yellow-green car bumper (probably that of a 1st-gen Cavalcade) is seen in a barn with a 2008 Liberty City license plate.

secrets.title: Liberty City Marathon
secrets.summary: NPCs around triathlons can occasionally be heard mentioning the Liberty City Marathon.

secrets.title: Liberty City Preachers
secrets.summary: Jerome, a soapbox preacher, may sometimes mention a brother in Liberty City. This is likely referencing the preachers that can be found around the map in GTA IV.

secrets.title: Morse Code Hatch
secrets.summary: By using the Submersible, players can find the famous hatch from the TV series Lost, which is located to the far east of the map, over the coast near the San Chianski Mountain Range. It is not possible to get up close to the hatch, as the player/submersible will be crushed by the water's pressure. If the player goes near the hatch, they will hear someone knocking on the other side. This is a message in Morse code...

secrets.title: Niko Bellic
secrets.summary: Within the Yellow Jack Inn is a framed portrait of Niko driving a tow truck. Scattered around the map, wanted posters with Niko's picture on them can be seen. Jimmy can sometimes be seen viewing Niko Bellic's LifeInvader page on his laptop while sitting at the dining table in his house. It is difficult to see the page in detail, however he appears to have Roman in his friends list and is stalking Burger Shot, which...

secrets.title: Roman's Taxis
secrets.summary: During one of the private fares for Downtown Cab Co, Franklin has to bring a passenger down to the docks to deal with The Lost MC bikers. They will be standing next to two Albany Emperors with license plates reading "NIKOB" and "ROMANB" - a reference to the Bellic cousins and also Roman's cab company, which used Albany vehicles (Esperantos and Cavalcades).

secrets.title: Shadey Petes Sunglasses
secrets.summary: A banner hanging outside Shadey Petes Sunglasses features an edited version of Lickingood's profile picture on the GTA IV in-game website Love Meet.

secrets.title: The Octopus
secrets.summary: At Elysian Island, a cargo ship known as the Octopus can be found docked. In GTA IV, it is located at Port Tudor, Alderney.

secrets.title: Three's Company
secrets.summary: The name of the mission Three's Company is possibly a reference to the GTA IV mission Three's a Crowd, as both feature Karen Daniels' first appearance in each game.

secrets.title: Trevor's CB radio
secrets.summary: Occasionally, if playing as Trevor and driving a vehicle with a CB radio, such as his Bodhi, the player may hear chatter over it. One of the conversations heard is between a security guard and a truck driver named Eddie Low. Low shares his name with a serial killer that could be found in Alderney by Niko in GTA IV, and acknowledges this during the conversation.

secrets.title: Vintage Liberty City
secrets.summary: Two of the in-game movies, Capolavoro and Meltdown, utilize recognizable locations from GTA IV, such as the Statue of Happiness, with the latter film inferred to take place there. Capolavoro also features the infamous Heart of Liberty City Easter egg and footage from Red Dead Redemption.

secrets.title: Yellow Jack Inn Poster
secrets.summary: A poster of a woman in a bikini can be found taped onto a wall in the Yellow Jack Inn. This poster first appeared in the Broker Safehouse in GTA IV.

secrets.title: Best of Show Awards
secrets.summary: At the Yellow Jack Inn, inside is a fridge and to the left is a wall with 4 trophy shields. The top 2 have the words 'Best Of Show 2008' and a picture of a motor bike. This refers to the release year of GTA IV and the expansion The Lost and Damned. The middle shield has the words 'Best Of Show 2010' with a picture of what appears to be a Stagecoach Wheel. This refers to Red Dead Redemption and its release year.

secrets.title: Johnny Klebitz Newspaper
secrets.summary: There are multiple newspapers scattered around the map with pictures of Johnny Klebitz from The Lost and Damned appearing on the cover, along with the headline "LOVE'S HATE RELATIONSHIP WITH THE TAXES".

secrets.title: Uptown Riders outfits
secrets.summary: In Franklin's wardrobe, several outfits containing the Uptown Riders logo can be found.

secrets.title: Buzzard Attack Chopper
secrets.summary: In Daddy's Little Girl, a Buzzard Attack Chopper can be seen flying towards the Dignity. This is likely a reference to the mission Sexy Time, from The Ballad of Gay Tony, during which the same type of helicopter is used to destroy a similar yacht.

secrets.title: Liberty City Popart
secrets.summary: Inside Franklin's mansion, a copy of Liberty City Popart can be seen stacked on a shelf. The picture on the cover first appeared as a painting within Yusuf Amir's Apartment in The Ballad of Gay Tony.

secrets.title: Luis Lopez License Plate
secrets.summary: In the same location as the "NIKOB" and "ROMANB" license plates (see above), there is also an LCC Hexer with a plate reading "LUISLOPZ" – a reference to The Ballad of Gay Tonys protagonist, Luis Fernando Lopez.

secrets.title: Yusuf Amir Luxury Finish
secrets.summary: The Yusuf Amir Luxury Finish that can be put on certain weapons in Ammu-Nation is named after Yusuf Amir, a character in The Ballad of Gay Tony. He finally makes an appearance in GTA Online in The Chop Shop update, which was released in December 2023.

secrets.title: GTA Online Protagonist
secrets.summary: In Casing the Jewel Store, Lester mentions that he is working with someone, but they're "too unpredictable" to hire as a heist crew member, likely referencing the GTA Online (though GTA Online was not released until two weeks after GTA V).

secrets.title: GTA V Multiplayer
secrets.summary: GTA V Multiplayer was meant to be the online component of GTA V before its plans were scrapped and replaced with GTA Online. Character models that were originally supposed to appear during a heist within the game, called the "Cops and Crooks Heist", can be found within photographs inside barber shops around the map.

secrets.title: Hopkins' Uniform
secrets.summary: In the Vanilla Unicorn strip club, an NPC will occasionally wear a blue jersey featuring the last name "Hopkins", which is the last name of Bullys protagonist.

secrets.title: Elysian Fields
secrets.summary: The Elysian Fields Freeway in the game is a reference to the Elysian Fields Development company from L.A. Noire.

secrets.title: Murderous Tattoo
secrets.summary: Franklin's neck tattoo, joining hands and a cross along with it, was first seen in L.A. Noire; it is the necklace of the murder victim in the homicide case "The Silk Stocking Murder". The protagonist in the featured game comes across it as a clue in a grocery store named "Just Picked Fruit Market".

secrets.title: Up-n-Atom
secrets.summary: One of the TV Commercials (for Up-n-Atom Burger) shows the restaurants as they were in 1950. The footage reuses images from L.A. Noire. Protagonist Cole Phelps and his Arson partner Herschel Biggs are shown as generic businessmen in the foreground.

secrets.title: Carcer City
secrets.summary: In the mission The Paleto Score, on the drive to the bank, Michael mentions that his first score was a heist in the outskirts of Carcer City in 1988, referring to an HD Universe counterpart of the city of the same name featured in Manhunt. Furthermore, Carcer Way is likely a reference to Carcer City, as well.

secrets.title: Boat
secrets.summary: The Dignity is extremely similar to, if not almost directly copied from the boat present in the beginning of the mission Sun Tan Oil, Stale Margaritas and Greed in Max Payne 3.

secrets.title: Max Payne's Outfit
secrets.summary: If Michael goes to a Sub Urban shop, he is able to buy a Hawaiian shirt very similar to the one Max Payne wears in Max Payne 3.

secrets.title: Café Redemption
secrets.summary: Café Redemption is likely a reference to Red Dead Redemption.

secrets.title: Capolavoro
secrets.summary: The in-game film Capolavoro uses locations from Red Dead Redemption.

secrets.title: De Santa Surname
secrets.summary: The surname "De Santa" that Michael Townley and his family took is a reference to Red Dead Redemption, an antagonist in Red Dead Redemption.

secrets.title: Escalera
secrets.summary: There is a Rent-A-Car agency named "Red Dead Redemption". Escalera is a town in Red Dead Redemption.

secrets.title: Hunting
secrets.summary: The Hunting side-activity appears to be based on the one that appears in Red Dead Redemption.

secrets.title: Red's Machine Supplies
secrets.summary: The sign of Red's Machine Supplies uses the "Chinese Rocks" font, which is also Red Dead Redemptions official font.

secrets.title: Red Dead-theme Artwork
secrets.summary: On the walls of Vinewood Self Storage - beneath the Olympic Freeway - is artwork resembling a silhouette of a cowboy riding a horse at night time, under a full moon. A second mural features cowboys taming wild horses with lasso. Both are likely references to Red Dead Redemption.

secrets.title: J. Marston the author
secrets.summary: On a book case in the living room of Franklin's Vinewood Hills house, there is a book titled Red Dead, by a J. Marston. "J. Marston" could refer to Red Dead Redemption, who regularly reads books and states that he may write a book himself one day.

secrets.title: John Marston T-Shirt
secrets.summary: During the mission Daddy's Little Girl, the man working at the bike rental shop in Vespucci Beach can be seen wearing a Red Dead Redemption t-shirt. Occasionally, NPCs can spawn around the map wearing this same shirt.

secrets.title: Mount Gordo
secrets.summary: The name of Mount Gordo is possibly a reference to Red Dead Redemption, a legendary animal from Red Dead Redemption.

secrets.title: New Austin Road Names
secrets.summary: There are two roads in Sandy Shores referencing towns in Red Dead Redemption, Cholla Springs Avenue and Armadillo Avenue.

secrets.title: The Last One
secrets.summary: The final mission unlocked in GTA V, The Last One, makes several references to the mission Red Dead Redemption from Red Dead Redemption. The GTA V Sasquatch Hunter shares the same appearance, voice, and personality as the Undead Nightmare Red Dead Redemption, though with slightly more modern clothes. He may also say "Gonna make my great grand-daddy proud", further referencing his counterpart. The hunter's name was...

secrets.title: Dune Buggy
secrets.summary: The ground-based Arms Trafficking missions could be a nod to the Smuggler's Run series, in which players must pick up and drop off contraband across the map. The Dune Buggy - which the GTA V missions are completed in - is a possible reference to some of the cars used in the series.

secrets.title: Assassin's Creed
secrets.summary: An EXsorbeo 720 videogame seen in Lester Crest's house, Assassin's Revenge, is a parody of the Assassin's Creed series.

secrets.title: BioShock
secrets.summary: An EXsorbeo 720 videogame seen in Lester Crest's house, Biocurse, is a parody of BioShock.

secrets.title: Borderlands
secrets.summary: Certain industrial and construction sites - such as Davis Quartz and Red's Machine Supplies - contain some sort of machine with paint art that resembles Claptrap from the video game series Borderlands.

secrets.title: Call of Duty
secrets.summary: The game Jimmy De Santa plays in his room is called Righteous Slaughter 7. It is a parody of modern shooters, mostly mocking the Call of Duty series (especially with it's later titles following Modern Warfare).

secrets.title: Dance Dance Revolution
secrets.summary: An EXsorbeo 720 videogame seen in Lester Crest's house, Dance Dance Maniac, is a parody of Dance Dance Revolution.

secrets.title: Dark Souls
secrets.summary: The gold medal objectives check list at the end of the mission Did Somebody Say Yoga? features a challenge named "Praise the Sun!". This is a reference to the Dark Souls series, a fantasy RPG, which features this line that has since attained meme-like popularity among Dark Souls fans. Furthermore, an EXsorbeo 720 videogame seen in Lester Crest's house, Hollow Soul, is likely a parody of Dark Souls.

secrets.title: Dead Island
secrets.summary: There are numerous billboards scattered around the game for the TV Show Rehab Island. The commercial for the TV shows can also be seen on the in-game television. The logo in the middle looks similar to the logo from the game Dead Island, with a marijuana leaf replacing the palm tree.

secrets.title: Dead Space/Mass Effect
secrets.summary: The EXsorbeo 720 videogame AlienProber3 is likely a reference to the Dead Space and Mass Effect franchises.

secrets.title: Dead Rising
secrets.summary: The drug Zombix is a reference to Zombrex from the Dead Rising series. Its tagline, "go straight for the head", further supports this.

secrets.title: DOOM/Fallout
secrets.summary: In a radio ad for Pride not Prejudice the announcer says that "some shooters are set in hell", referencing the Doom series, and "others are set in post-apocalyptic wastelands", possibly referencing the Fallout series. Additionally, the rocket found at the Procopio Truck Stop is possibly a reference to the rocket souvenir from Fallout: New Vegas. When next to the rocket, sounds of a Geiger counter can be heard...

secrets.title: Duke Nukem/Gears of War
secrets.summary: In Floyd's Apartment, there is a mural which originally reads "Live, Love, Laugh", over which Trevor writes "Eat, Shit, Die". This is a possible reference to Duke Nukem's signature phrase "Eat shit and Die". Furthermore, this could be a reference to the Gears of War series, where it is possible hear this phrase when executing a Locust.

secrets.title: God of War
secrets.summary: An EXsorbeo 720 videogame seen in Lester Crest's house, Fog of War 2, is a parody of God of War II.

secrets.title: Mario
secrets.summary: Two garden mushrooms can be seen in Denise Clinton's house, a short red mushroom and a tall green one, which is likely a reference to Mario and Luigi in the Super Mario series.

secrets.title: Mortal Kombat
secrets.summary: A natural rock formation in the Grand Senora Desert named Tremor's Rock is likely a reference to Tremor in the Mortal Kombat franchise, known for his ability to manipulate rocks and to enhance himself with rock formations on his body.

secrets.title: PGA Tour
secrets.summary: An EXsorbeo 720 videogame seen in Lester Crest's house, Golf: Wood In The Rough, is a parody of the PGA Tour series.

secrets.title: Portal
secrets.summary: There is graffiti in an alleyway in Downtown Vinewood (where the mission Bearing the Truth starts) on which, amongst multiple Kifflom rambles, is written "The fruit tree is a lie", referencing the iconic "The cake is a lie" catchphrase from the Portal series and possibly comparing it to the fruit tree in the Adam and Eve creation theory, which the Epsilon Program disregard.

secrets.title: Saints Row
secrets.summary: NPCs can sometimes be heard saying "City of saints gonna struggle, Los Santos ain't in no trouble", referencing the videogame series Saints Row and its rivalry with the Grand Theft Auto series.

secrets.title: SimCity
secrets.summary: An EXsorbeo 720 videogame seen in Lester Crest's house, Simplecity, is a parody of SimCity.

secrets.title: Sonic the Hedgehog
secrets.summary: There is a business called "Supersonic" located in Downtown Los Santos, with the motto "The Ultra Fast Ring Service". This is a reference to the Sonic the Hedgehog franchise.

secrets.title: Street Fighter
secrets.summary: The Akuma is a Japanese motorcycle with a "streetfighter" style body. In the Street Fighter series, Akuma is featured as a hidden boss and later as a playable character (coincidentally, Capcom publishes the GTA series, along with Street Fighter, in Japan).

secrets.title: 2001: A Space Odyssey/Aliens/The Big Lebowski
secrets.summary: The trip sequence in the mission Did Somebody Say Yoga? references multiple Hollywood movies: It resembles Stanley Kubrick's 2001: A Space Odyssey - similar to the beginning of the trip, the movie starts with apes, which represent early humans, and ends with the protagonist going out of a spaceship into a colorful and trippy "star-gate". The appearance of the aliens that abduct Michael and often appear recurrently...

secrets.title: 8½/Andrei Rublev/Persona
secrets.summary: Capolavoro mostly references and parodies 1960s European cinema, with some distinguishable influences. The cinematography is extremely similar to that seen in Federico Fellini's 8½. The use of horses as recurrent symbolism is likely a nod to Tarkovsky's Andrei Rublev. It shares similarities with Ingmar Begman's Persona, notably the use of a seemingly disjointed dream sequence as an introduction and the reflections...

secrets.title: A Boy and His Dog/Lassie
secrets.summary: The dog that Franklin speaks to during Risk Assessment could possibly be a reference to the famous dog Lassie. It could also be a reference to the movie A Boy and His Dog.

secrets.title: A Bug's Life
secrets.summary: One of the gold medal requirements for The Jewel Store Job's Smart Approach is called "It's A Bug's Death", referencing the movie A Bug's Life.

secrets.title: A Nightmare on Elm Street
secrets.summary: One of Merle Abrahams' poems (see above) within Senora National Park reads: "One is done, Two was fun, Three tried to run, Four called mom, Five's not alive, Six is nix, Seven's in heaven, 8 won't wait." This may be a reference to Freddy Krueger's poem from the Nightmare on Elm Street franchise.

secrets.title: Air Force One
secrets.summary: In Minor Turbulence, the cargo plane's pilot may shout "get off my plane!", referencing a famous line from Air Force One.

secrets.title: Akira
secrets.summary: The description of the Vindicator states that the vehicle was "bold and futuristic when you first saw these feet forwards motorcycles in 80s anime". This is a reference to the 1988 Japanese animation Akira, in which protagonist Kaneda rides an iconic retro futuristic bike. Said bike was stated to be one of the major design influences of the Honda NM4, the motorcycle on which the Vindicator mostly takes inspiration...

secrets.title: Aliens
secrets.summary: In Los Santos, the museum called Bishop's WTF?!, an obvious parody of the famous Ripley's Believe It Or Not! museums, can be found. Ripley and Bishop are both central characters in the 1986 film Aliens.

secrets.title: American History X/Harry Potter
secrets.summary: A book named American History Y can be seen in 3671 Whispymound Drive. This is a reference to the 1998 movie American History X. Additionally, its author is stated to be "H. Potter", likely referencing the character Harry Potter from the series of the same name.

secrets.title: American Zombie
secrets.summary: The poster and name of the Vinewood classic film Vinewood Zombie parody that of the 2007 film American Zombie.

secrets.title: Back to the Future
secrets.summary: Some power stations have an orange sticker that says 1.21 GW (GW most likely an abbreviation of gigawatt), a reference to the Back to the Future trilogy. There are two churches (one in Pacific Bluffs and the other in Great Chaparral) called Hill Valley Church. This is another reference to the Back to the Future trilogy, as the three movies take place in a fictitious Californian town called Hill Valley.

secrets.title: Battle: Los Angeles/Independence Day
secrets.summary: During an optional tour in Downtown Vinewood, the Vinewood Tour lady will state that the mayor's office appeared during a "twenty-minute final dogfight to save Earth" in the movie Invasion: Los Santos. The "dogfight to save Earth" is a reference to 1996 alien invasion movie Independence Day, which ends with a lengthy dogfight sequence, while the title "Invasion: Los Santos" is a reference to another alien invasion...

secrets.title: Beverly Hills Cop
secrets.summary: The Jewel Store Job's loud approach appears to be loosely inspired by the opening scene of Beverly Hills Cop II.

secrets.title: Blade Runner
secrets.summary: The title of the movie The Shoulder of Orion II is a reference to the line "Attack ships on fire off the shoulder of Orion", part of the famous "Tears in Rain" monologue in the 1982 film Blade Runner.

secrets.title: Blues Brothers
secrets.summary: The cashier in an Ammu-Nation stores may mention "a pregnant lady who bought a flamethrower earlier", referencing The Blues Brothers. Additionally, the movie is referenced by the name of the pop duo, Blue Brothers.

secrets.title: Cool Hand Luke
secrets.summary: The name of the motor oil and engine lubricant business, Coolhand Lube, is a reference to the 1967 movie Cool Hand Luke.

secrets.title: Die Hard With a Vengeance/Mission Impossible
secrets.summary: The Obvious Approach to The Big Score is a reference to the 1995 film Die Hard With a Vengeance. Both involve characters stealing gold bullion by drilling through a wall with a tunneling machine at a nearby under construction subway station. Furthermore, the helicopter chase through the Ron Alternates Wind Farm is likely inspired by a similar scene in Mission Impossible III. Both also include missiles being fired...

secrets.title: Dragonheart
secrets.summary: The movie Dragon Brain, which can be found mentioned on flyers around the map, is likely a reference to Dragonheart.

secrets.title: Drive
secrets.summary: If the player goes to any Binco or Discount Store as Trevor, there is a jacket called "Champagne Driver Blouson," which has a crab on the back. This is a reference to the movie Drive, as the main character wore the same jacket, with the only difference being that there was a scorpion on the back.

secrets.title: Enemy of the State/True Romance
secrets.summary: The Mexican standoff in the mission The Wrap Up is inspired by the films Enemy of the State and True Romance.

secrets.title: Flip the Frog
secrets.summary: The animated film Bip The Dog is a play on the character Flip the Frog, who starred in a series of cartoons in the early 1930s.

secrets.title: Friday the 13th
secrets.summary: The White Hockey Mask that can be purchased at Vespucci Movie Masks is a major reference to Jason Voorhees, the main protagonist of the Friday the 13th slasher film series. Additionally, the gold medal requirement for the mission Masks, which requires the player to purchase three White Hockey Masks, is titled "Cliche", further refencing the series. Furthermore, the Knife After Dark film appears to be a parody of the...

secrets.title: Gone in 60 Seconds
secrets.summary: In Hayes Autos, written on a wall is a list of cars to be stolen for Devin Weston that can only be seen in UV light. This is likely a reference to the movie Gone in 60 Seconds.

secrets.title: Ghostbusters
secrets.summary: The Digiscanner bears a strong resemblance, both in appearance and function, to the P.K.E. Meter, a device in the Ghostbusters movies.

secrets.title: Heat
secrets.summary: The theme of major heists in GTA V is heavily inspired by the 1995 film Heat, which is set in Los Angeles, the city Los Santos is based on. Michael De Santa seems to take loose inspiration from the film's main character, Neil McCauley, as both are seasoned bank robbers and leaders of crews; in fact, Michael's default gray suit is virtually identical to one that McCauley wears prominently during the film....

secrets.title: Hot Rod
secrets.summary: The brand name of the coffeehouse chain Cool Beans may be a reference to a scene from the cult comedy film Hot Rod, where the words "cool beans" are repeated numerous times.

secrets.title: I Am Number Four
secrets.summary: Trevor walking away from the exploding O'Neil farmhouse in Crystal Maze references a similar scene in the movie I Am Number Four.

secrets.title: Indiana Jones
secrets.summary: A hat found on a chair within Solomon Richards' office resembles the iconic one worn by Indiana Jones in the series of the same name.

secrets.title: Jackie Brown
secrets.summary: Floyd's apartment, Trevor's first safehouse in Los Santos, is modeled upon Melanie's apartment from the movie Jackie Brown by Quentin Tarantino. Even the pictures on the kitchen's pillar are very similar to those depicted in the movie.

secrets.title: James Bond
secrets.summary: There is a customized JB 700 armed with machine guns, tire spikes and a passenger ejector seat in the mission "Deep Inside" for Devin Weston. This is a reference to James Bond's specially modified Aston Martin DB5 (on which the JB 700 is modeled) from the 1964 movie Goldfinger. The in-game business "J's Bonds" could also be a reference to the main protagonist of the 007 franchise, James Bond. Furthermore, the...

secrets.title: Jaws
secrets.summary: The description for the Out of Your Depth achievement is "You're gonna need a bigger boat...", referencing a famous line from the movie Jaws. Furthermore, a flyer attached to a noticeboard at the Sonar Collections Dock asking the reader if they "need a bigger boat"; and one of Sharkies Bites's mottos, "you're gonna need a bigger bite"; also reference the line.

secrets.title: Jurassic Park
secrets.summary: When asking a taxi driver to go faster, he may reply with "Hold on to your butt!", a line from Jurassic Park.

secrets.title: Kill Bill
secrets.summary: In Keyla's private taxi fare, her cheating fiancé drives a Bison with the license plate "PUSSYWAG", referencing the Pussy Wagon from Kill Bill.

secrets.title: King Kong/Nineteen Eighty-Four/Treasure Island/WALL-E
secrets.summary: The in-game movie The Loneliest Robot in Great Britain references several films. Overall, it seems to take inspiration from the movies Nineteen Eighty-Four - itself adapted from George Orwell's book of the same name - and WALL-E. The former takes place in a dystopic Great Britain with an authoritarian government, and the latter depicts a lonely robot on a futuristic Earth, both of which are major themes of the...

secrets.title: Law Abiding Citizen
secrets.summary: Jay Norris' death in Friend Request is likely a reference to the movie Law Abiding Citizen, during which a character is killed upon answering a phone that promptly explodes next to their head.

secrets.title: Lethal Weapon
secrets.summary: In Marriage Counseling, Michael destroying the deck of Martin Madrazo's Vinewood Hills house by attaching a pickup truck winch to one of the support columns is a reference to a scene in the movie Lethal Weapon 2.

secrets.title: Midnight Cowboy
secrets.summary: In "Minor Turbulence", Trevor may shout "I'm flying here!" while approaching the cargo plane, referencing the famous line, "I'm walking here!" from the 1969 movie Midnight Cowboy.

secrets.title: No Country for Old Men
secrets.summary: If the player goes to the Chiliad Mountain State Wilderness just off of U.S. Route 1, there will be a Random Event revolving around a drug deal having gone bad. The player will find a briefcase, several corpses, and a man on the ground who tells them to "stay away from the case." If the case is grabbed (which adds $25,000 to the player's in-game account), the man will still say that the player is "a dead man". Later...

secrets.title: Pee-wee's Big Adventure
secrets.summary: The music that plays in the mission Grass Roots - Trevor, during which he fights clowns in a drug-induced hallucination, is inspired by music that plays during the evil clown dream scene in Pee-wee's Big Adventure.

secrets.title: Predator
secrets.summary: The mission Predator is a reference to the Predator movie franchise, in which the predator hunts humans with the use of thermal vision.

secrets.title: Psycho
secrets.summary: At the Sonar Collections Dock near Paleto Bay, there is a noticeboard showing multiple ads. One of them says "Norman Baits - The Mother of all catches!" This is a reference to Alfred Hitchcock's Psycho, and the leading character, Norman Bates', relationship with his mother, Norma.

secrets.title: Rambo
secrets.summary: A soapboxer named Clinton, who is a veteran suffering from PTSD, claims that he once put a knife in his teeth and killed a large number of enemy combatants with it, referencing the Rambo series.

secrets.title: Saw
secrets.summary: The movie Water Torture IX is a reference to the Saw franchise.

secrets.title: Sequel to the Sequel
secrets.summary: A movie can be seen advertised called Sequel II. The title, number and tagline is a joke on movie sequels in general. A similar joke is used in Rockstar Vancouver's Bully.

secrets.title: Spider-Man
secrets.summary: During Did Somebody Say Yoga?, Jimmy refers to Ahron Ward as the "friendly neighborhood drug dealer", referencing the "friendly neighborhood Spider-Man" catchphrase from the Spider-Man franchise.

secrets.title: Star Trek
secrets.summary: At Silent Probe Mountain, the words "Beam Me Up" are written, which is a reference to the often-misquoted "Beam me up, Scotty" phrase attributed to James T. Kirk when wanting to be transported back to the Starship Enterprise in Star Trek. In Monkey Business, Steve Haines may instruct Michael to use a Stun Gun by telling him to "set [his] phaser to stun".

secrets.title: Star Wars
secrets.summary: There is an outdoor ad for a Drone Chatterbot smartphone, bearing the slogan "this is the drone you've been looking for". This is an obvious reference to the line "these aren't the droids you're looking for" from Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope. Lester Crest also references this line in the mission Cleaning out the Bureau, saying "this is not the car we're looking for".

secrets.title: The A-Team
secrets.summary: The mission Three's Company appears to be partially inspired by the movie The A-Team.

secrets.title: The Godfather
secrets.summary: If playing as Michael while rescuing Antonia Bottino during her random event, she will ask for his name. Michael responds by questioning whether of not he will find a severed horse head in his bed the following morning, referencing a scene in The Godfather.

secrets.title: The Howling
secrets.summary: The Growling is a parody of the 1981 movie The Howling.

secrets.title: The Italian Job
secrets.summary: The subtle approach of the heist mission The Big Score is a reference to the film The Italian Job, where three Mini Coopers are used to carry out a heist to steal gold bars. While the game uses four Gauntlets instead, both involve armored trucks and manipulating the traffic light system.

secrets.title: The Lord of the Rings
secrets.summary: During the bike race with Jimmy in Daddy's Little Girl, Jimmy may say "you shall not pass!" while attempting to ride by him, referencing a popular line from The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring.

secrets.title: The Matrix
secrets.summary: There is a green-ish filter in the Rockstar Editor named "Morpheus". This could be a reference to the 1999 movie The Matrix, in which Morpheus was a major character, reflecting the movie's distinctive green-filtered aesthetics. The Übermacht cars Oracle, Zion, and Sentinel are also references to The Matrix. The Oracle refers to the computer program that helps humans fight the machines, the Zion refers to the last...

secrets.title: The Shining
secrets.summary: In one of the discount stores or Binco, it is possible to find a red jacket named "Overlooked Red Blouson" for Trevor, which is the jacket worn by Jack Torrance in the movie The Shining. The hotel where the Torrance family stays in the movie is also called The Overlook Hotel.

secrets.title: Thelma and Louise
secrets.summary: In the mountains there is a Thelma and Louise Easter egg. If the player goes to a specific point between 7:00 and 8:00 PM, they will see a vehicle similar to the one from the movie. A few feet behind the vehicle are several law enforcement personnel, police cars, and a helicopter. When one of the officers begins to approach the vehicle, its engine starts and the car drives off of the edge of the cliff. This Easter...

secrets.title: Top Gun
secrets.summary: Fort Zancudo's beta name, as heard via unused police scanner dialogue found in the game files, is Kazansky Air-Force Base, referencing the character Tom Kazansky from Top Gun.

secrets.title: Under Siege
secrets.summary: In the mission Derailed, the cutscene of the two trains colliding on the Raton Canyon Bridge and falling into the creek below is identical to a scene from the 1995 movie Under Siege 2: Dark Territory.

secrets.title: Wall Street/Office Space
secrets.summary: The film Meltdown is a parody of Wall Street. Additionally, its tagline "He didn't get the memo" is possibly a reference to Office Space.

secrets.title: Wayne's World
secrets.summary: During the Stag Do Running Man random event, the groom's bride will call him a "psycho hose beast", referencing an insult used by the protagonist of Wayne's World to refer to his ex-girlfriend. Additionally, in Vinewood Souvenirs - Nigel and Mrs. Thornhill, both Nigel and Mrs. Thornhill bow down to Trevor while chanting "we're not worthy", further referencing the film.

secrets.title: Wilhelm Scream
secrets.summary: While inside Richards Majestic Productions studios, it is possible to hear the Wilhelm scream, which is a very famous stock sound effect that has been used in more than 200 movies, beginning in 1951 for the film Distant Drums. It is also used during the mission Father/Son when Franklin throws one of the thieves off Michael's stolen yacht during the highway battle.

secrets.title: ALF/My Two Dads
secrets.summary: On the in-game website theinternetisahellhole.com, the site states "You remember sitting in front of the TV as a kid - watching a magical world where every kind of problem was solved within an hour. Families were funny and sometimes had pet aliens or two parents of the same sex but were all heterosexual.". These are allusions to both the television series ALF and My Two Dads, respectively.

secrets.title: Barney & Friends
secrets.summary: In Blaine County, the purple dinosaur at Rex's Diner resembles Barney from the childrens' show Barney & Friends.

secrets.title: Brass Eye
secrets.summary: Good Aids Pharmacy is a reference to the British satirical show Brass Eye, where the host in one episode speaks out in support of people with "good AIDS" (who caught the virus 'through no fault of their own') and condemning those who have "bad AIDS" (who caught it through having gay sex or drug abuse).

secrets.title: Breaking Bad
secrets.summary: Trevor's calculator watch is a nod to Walter White from Breaking Bad, as both wear the exact same watch and are in the methamphetamine business. The in-game website Cashfordeaddreams.com further references the show, as the description of the RV claims that "gourmet pharmaceutical bakers" like to use them to drive into the middle of nowhere to "practice their craft".

secrets.title: Cartoon Network
secrets.summary: There is a car tuning garage close to the Vanilla Unicorn called Car Tune Network. This is a reference to the Cartoon Network TV channel.

secrets.title: CHiPs
secrets.summary: The mission I Fought the Law... is inspired by the show CHiPs, which follows the lives of two California Highway Patrol motorcycle officers. Additionally, the mission's soundtrack is internally named "alc_car_steal_1_chips", further supporting the reference.

secrets.title: Dexter
secrets.summary: In the mission Dead Man Walking, there is a paper on a corkboard on the top floor with two names on it: Dexter Fisher and Morgan Price, possibly a reference to Dexter Morgan. Fisher-Price is also a major American toy manufacturer.

secrets.title: Digimon
secrets.summary: On the radio station West Coast Classics, DJ Pooh talks about a new smartphone app called Digipun. This may be a reference to the animated series Digimon.

secrets.title: Initial D
secrets.summary: In the Tuner section of the available wheels in Los Santos Customs, there is a design called "Fujiwara" - a clear nod to the Initial D manga/anime protagonist Takumi Fujiwara. The wheel design is also identical to the design used his car, a Toyota Corolla "Sprinter" Trueno AE86, used in the series.

secrets.title: Magnum, P.I.
secrets.summary: The Tropical Shirt that can be bought by Michael in Sub Urban is similar looking to the one worn by Magnum on the show Magnum, P.I.

secrets.title: The Boondocks
secrets.summary: Random pedestrians can sometimes be heard saying "I sent that bitch a smiley face, bitches love smiley faces!", referencing the popular line from the show The Boondocks.

secrets.title: The Sopranos
secrets.summary: Michael De Santa appears to be heavily inspired by the character Tony Soprano from The Sopranos, as they share many similarities. Notable examples among others are that both see a psychiatrist, both have an ungrateful son who owns a yellow SUV, both are fans of classic cinema, both have protégés they view as the son they never had, and both destroy an electronic belonging of their son at a point when they were under...

secrets.title: The Walking Dead
secrets.summary: Two of the deputy sheriffs that appear in the mission The Paleto Score are named Grimes and Kirkman, which is a reference to Rick Grimes and Robert Kirkman, the protagonist and author of the popular comic book and TV series The Walking Dead, respectively. Additionally, in the Fire Crew approach of The Bureau Raid, an FIB agent can refer to Michael disguised as a janitor as the "mopping dead".

secrets.title: X-Files
secrets.summary: A poster can be found inside Lester's House, depicting a flying saucer and the phrase "Accept the truth", a reference to Fox Mulder's "I Want to Believe" poster in The X-Files.

secrets.title: American Idiot
secrets.summary: The design used for the Organ Farm billboard depicts a clutched bleeding heart similar to the one depicted on the cover of the Green Day album, American Idiot.

secrets.title: "Arirang"
secrets.summary: Arirang Plaza references the Korean folk song, "Arirang".

secrets.title: Gangnam Style/Psy
secrets.summary: The character Kwak and his song "Bitchz Got Seoul" is a reference to the South Korean singer Psy and his song "Gangnam Style".

secrets.title: "I Fought the Law"
secrets.summary: The name of the mission "I Fought the Law..." is a reference to the song of the same name, written by Sonny Curtis and popularized by The Bobby Fuller Four.

secrets.title: "I'm on a Boat"
secrets.summary: There is a calendar featured in multiple locations with a picture of a Reefer and a caption saying "I'm on a boat!", referencing the Lonely Island song "I'm on a Boat".

secrets.title: "Inmates (We're All Crazy)"
secrets.summary: During Crystal Maze, Trevor will shout "You're all deeeaaad". Due to how it is enunciated, it is likely a reference to the Alice Cooper song "Inmates (We're All Crazy)".

secrets.title: "Karma Chameleon"
secrets.summary: In Vinewood, graffiti written on a wall that states "Karma - it's a chameleon" can be found. This is a reference to the song "Karma Chameleon" by Culture Club.

secrets.title: "Stockholm Syndrome"
secrets.summary: In the beginning of the mission Derailed, Michael makes a sarcastic remark about Stockholm syndrome, claiming it is "very nice this time of year" as Trevor and Patricia enter the trailer. Rather than the psychological phenomenon, this is a reference to the 2003 rock song "[https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_Syndrome_(Muse_song) Stockholm Syndrome]" by the English rock band...

secrets.title: "Purple Haze"
secrets.summary: The "Purple Haze" filter in the Rockstar Editor is a reference to the eponymous Jimi Hendrix song.

secrets.title: "Rapper's Delight"
secrets.summary: The store Snapper's Delight in the Chamberlain Hills Shopping Plaza is a reference to the 1979 song "Rapper's Delight" by The Sugarhill Gang.

secrets.title: The Power Station
secrets.summary: The Palmer-Taylor Power Station is a reference to the 1980s supergroup The Power Station, which featured members Robert Palmer, John Taylor and Andy Taylor.

secrets.title: "The Revolution Will Not Be Televised"
secrets.summary: During the shootout at the Altruist Camp, one of the cult members will yell "The new boom will not be televised!", referencing the song by Gil Scott-Heron, "The Revolution Will Not Be Televised".

secrets.title: "The Teddy Bear's Picnic"
secrets.summary: In a switch scene after Lamar Down, Trevor will say, "If you go out in the woods today, prepare for a big surprise...", referencing a similar line from the 1932 song "The Teddy Bears' Picnic".

secrets.title: Twelve Angry Men
secrets.summary: A book named "Twelve Hungry Women" can be seen in 3671 Whispymound Drive. This is a reference to the 1954 drama Twelve Angry Men.

secrets.title: "U Can't Touch This"
secrets.summary: The gold medal requirement called "Can't Touch This" for the mission Complications is a reference to the song "U Can't Touch This" by MC Hammer.

secrets.title: A Song of Ice and Fire
secrets.summary: In certain situations, a female pedestrian can be heard shouting "Seven hells!", which is a common saying in the A Song of Ice and Fire book series by George R. R. Martin.

secrets.title: Farmer Giles of Ham
secrets.summary: The name of the store Farmer Giles references the 1949 book Farmer Giles of Ham by J. R. R. Tolkien.

secrets.title: Fifty Shades
secrets.summary: The Intimacy trilogy, written by Terry Bolan, is a parody of the E.L. James Fifty Shades trilogy.

secrets.title: Grantland Rice
secrets.summary: A mural can be found in Textile City containing the Grantland Rice poem "Alumnus Football" written around it.

secrets.title: Greek mythology
secrets.summary: Various references are made to Greek mythology throughout GTA V. *The Sisyphus Theater is named after the character Sisyphus, a king who is forced to push a boulder up a hill, only to watch it roll back down, everyday for eternity. *The Elysian Fields Freeway references the Elysian Fields, said to be the section of the underworld in which the heroic dead reside. *As evidenced by their logo, the automotive...

secrets.title: Hamlet
secrets.summary: After buying the McKenzie Field Hangar, it is possible to switch to Trevor and find him standing in front of it, saying "to work, or not to work?" This is a reference to a famous line from William Shakespeare's tragedy Hamlet, "to be, or not to be".

secrets.title: Histoire de Charles Martel
secrets.summary: A painting in the Yellow Jack Inn is taken from an in a page of the medieval book Histoire de Charles Martel.

secrets.title: Irish mythology
secrets.summary: The Banshee is named after a female spirit seen as an omen of death in Irish mythology.

secrets.title: Kama Sutra
secrets.summary: In Michael's bedroom, there is a copy of The Kama Sutra on the night table, a reference to the real life book of the same name.

secrets.title: Las sergas de Esplandián
secrets.summary: Calafia Road, North Calafia Way, and the Calafia Bridge are named after the fictional warrior queen Calafia from the 1510 novel Las sergas de Esplandián by Garci Rodríguez de Montalvo, in which she is the ruler of a kingdom of black women living on the mythical Island of California.

secrets.title: Norse mythology
secrets.summary: The vehicle Kraken and its manufacturer Kraken Submersibles are named after a large sea monster from Norse mythology.

secrets.title: Our American Cousin
secrets.summary: The name of the vehicle company Dundreary appears to be based on Lord Dundreary, a character from the 1858 play Our American Cousin. Further supporting this, the company is based on the real life Lincoln Motor Company, and the aforementioned play was what President Abraham Lincoln was watching when he was assassinated.

secrets.title: Paradise Lost
secrets.summary: The original name for the mission Hang Ten was "Paradise Lost", referencing the epic poem of the same name by John Milton.

secrets.title: The Autobiography of Malcolm X
secrets.summary: A book inside Franklin's mansion has "Malcolm Eggs" written along the spine, referencing The Autobiography of Malcolm X.

secrets.title: The Bible
secrets.summary: In "Marriage Counseling", Michael quotes the biblical verse "It's a foolish man who builds his house in sand", which Franklin recognizes as belonging to the Gospel of Matthew. The Leviathan is named after the eponymous sea monster from the Old Testament. The pet food company Animal Ark is a reference to the biblical story of Noah's Ark.

secrets.title: The Grapes of Wrath
secrets.summary: Joad Lane is named after the Joad family from the novel The Grapes of Wrath. Furthering this allusion is that the road is located in Grapeseed, and the original book's plot involves a family travelling to California.

secrets.title: Three wise monkeys
secrets.summary: In the setup for Blitz Play, upon Dave Norton stating that some of the government is corrupt, Michael, Franklin, and Trevor perform the Three wise monkeys pose (see, hear, speak no evil).

secrets.title: Vanity Fair
secrets.summary: In 3671 Whispymound Drive, a book can be seen on the shelf titled Vanity Unfair. This is likely a reference to the 1848 novel Vanity Fair by William Makepeace Thackeray.

secrets.title: We're Going on a Bear Hunt
secrets.summary: While approaching a passing train in Caida Libre, Trevor may say "Can't go round the train, gotta go over it." This is possibly a reference to the children's book We're Going on a Bear Hunt.

secrets.title: Wuthering Heights
secrets.summary: A book inside Franklin's mansion is titled Wither Heights, likely referencing the book Wuthering Heights by Emily Brontë.

secrets.title: 4PlayerPodcast
secrets.summary: Sometimes when switching to Trevor while not on a mission, he and another man in front of him will be riding a Faggio and Trevor will say, "We are scooter brothers! Scooooter brothers!" This is a reference to 4PP .

secrets.title: Action Figures
secrets.summary: Inside Lester's safehouse, to the right of his bedroom, there are some action figures that closely resemble Master Chief from Halo, Superman and Black Adam from the DC Universe, presumably Han Solo from Star Wars and two other figures. Below the figures is a replica of the Excalibur sword.

secrets.title: Courage Wolf
secrets.summary: The design of the Special Airborne Unit logo features the "Courage Wolf" internet meme.

secrets.title: Get A Brain! Morans
secrets.summary: At an intersection in South Los Santos and on a house along Route 68, a handwritten sign can be found that reads, "IMPEACH THE SOCIALIST" and "GET A BRIAN YOU MORANS". The latter is a reference to a popular photograph of a man at a protest in Saint Charles, Missouri, holding a sign reading "Get a BRAIN! MORANS". The photograph became widely spread due to the ironic misspelling of the word "morons".

secrets.title: Goatse
secrets.summary: Some taxi cabs will spawn with the license plate "80AAT533", referencing the internet meme "Goatse".

secrets.title: I Like Turtles
secrets.summary: NPCs in Blaine County may occasionally say "I like turtles", referencing the meme of the same name.

secrets.title: Reddit
secrets.summary: The article title "Narwhal Bacon?" can be seen on several trash and newspaper box copies of the Daily Rag and Las Mentiras newspapers. This is a reference to the phrase "The Narwhal bacons at midnight", a phrase coined by Redditors to identify each other.

secrets.title: Alco Holla
secrets.summary: The name of the drink Alco Holla is an obvious play on the word "alcohol".

secrets.title: Anna Rex/Bull Emic
secrets.summary: The clothing companies Anna Rex and Bull Emic are plays on "anorexic" and "bulimic", which are terms used to describe someone with the eating disorders, anorexia and bulimia, respectively.

secrets.title: Biglogs Corp.
secrets.summary: The name of the cereal company, Biglogs, is a reference to feces.

secrets.title: Brownstreak
secrets.summary: An EXsorbeo 720 game seen in Lester Crest's house, Brownstreak, is a reference to feces skidmarks.

secrets.title: Bullshot Dartboards
secrets.summary: The "Bullshot" in Bullshot Dartboards is likely a play on the term "bullshit".

secrets.title: Caca
secrets.summary: The name of the fashion brand, Caca, translates to "poop" in Portuguese, Spanish, Romanian, Russian, and French. Additionally, the words "cherish it" appear in an advertisement for the brand, but are stylized to also read as "cheri shit".

secrets.title: Cart-L
secrets.summary: The name of the business chain Cart-L is an obvious play on the word "cartel".

secrets.title: Crystal Heights
secrets.summary: The apartment complex Crystal Heights is a play on the drug crystal meth and getting high.

secrets.title: Deals & Dollars
secrets.summary: The name of Deals & Dollars is a double entendre; while it could mean that the company sells items for cheap deals, it may also be a reference to drug dealing.

secrets.title: Designer Slave
secrets.summary: Designer Slave is possibly a reference to sweatshops.

secrets.title: ECola
secrets.summary: The soft drink ECola is a reference to both E. coli bacteria and the Ebola virus. This is further backed up by their slogan, "deliciously infectious", and a subway advertisement depicting bacteria coming out of an ECola bottle.

secrets.title: Enema
secrets.summary: The high-end fashion store, Enema, is an obvious reference to the act of the same name, which involves one cleaning their colon by pumping water into it.

secrets.title: Flickers Comics
secrets.summary: The "Flickers" in Flickers Comics can be read as "Fuckers" in certain fonts.

secrets.title: Fuque
secrets.summary: The name of the store, Fuque, is a clear play on the word "fuck".

secrets.title: Hawaiian Snow
secrets.summary: The clothing store Hawaiian Snow shares its name with slang for marijuana seeds.

secrets.title: Hung Drawn & Quarters
secrets.summary: The name of the arcade Hung Drawn & Quarters is a reference to hanging, drawing, and quartering; a torturous capital punishment for high treason in medieval England.

secrets.title: Internet Cursor
secrets.summary: While hovering over a clickable link within the in-game internet, the cursor will turn into a middle finger, rather than a traditional pointer finger.

secrets.title: Klepto's Pawn Store
secrets.summary: Klepto's Pawn Store is a reference to kleptomania.

secrets.title: Krapea
secrets.summary: Krapea, a furniture manufacturer, is a play on the word "crap".

secrets.title: Limey's Juice and Smoothies
secrets.summary: The "limey's" in Limey's Juice and Smoothies is a reference to a derogatory term for British people.

secrets.title: LS Benders
secrets.summary: The LS Benders reference the term "bender", meaning when a person goes on a nonstop binge of drugs or alcohol, lasting for a full day or more.

secrets.title: Lucky Plucker
secrets.summary: The name of the fast food chain Lucky Plucker is a play on the term "lucky fucker". Additionally, their menu boards in the enhanced edition have the word "cock" throughout them.

secrets.title: Noodle Exchange
secrets.summary: Noodle Exchange is a play on the term "needle exchange", which is when drug users swap out used needles for new ones.

secrets.title: Opium Nights/Poppy House
secrets.summary: The hotel Opium Nights and the connecting restaurant Poppy House reference the drug opium and the plant from which it's made from.

secrets.title: Pharte Air/Pharte Gas
secrets.summary: The names of Pharte Air and Pharte Gas are meant to sound like "fart air" and "fart gas", respectively, when said aloud. This is further reinforced by Pharte Gas' tagline, "It's perfectly natural", and their guarantee that "Pharte Gas is farmed from humans by humans".

secrets.title: Pop's Pills
secrets.summary: The name of the pharmaceutical company Pop's Pills is meant to reference "popping pills", which is slang for consuming ecstasy.

secrets.title: Pißwasser
secrets.summary: The name of the alcohol company Pißwasser is German for "piss water".

secrets.title: Rogers Salvage & Scrap Motto
secrets.summary: The motto of Rogers Salvage & Scrap, "taking your scrap since 1924", is a play on "taking your crap".

secrets.title: Sheet Yourself Laundromat
secrets.summary: The "Sheet Yourself" in Sheet Yourself Laundromat is a play on the phrase "shit yourself".

secrets.title: Shitzu
secrets.summary: The Japanese company Shitzu is a reference to feces, due to the word "shit" appearing in its name and the company's logo appearing to depict a pile of it.

secrets.title: Sod Off
secrets.summary: The name of the agrochemical manufacturing company, Sod Off, is British slang meaning "piss off".

secrets.title: Stoner Cement Works
secrets.summary: The "Stoner" in Stoner Cement Works references slang for a person who often does weed.

secrets.title: Tinkle/Whiz
secrets.summary: Both Tinkle and Whiz are cellphone companies with names referencing urinating. This is further supported by Tinkle's logo appearing to feature a drop of urine, and an advertisement saying "take a Whiz anywhere".

secrets.title: With a Paddle White Water Activity Center
secrets.summary: The name of With a Paddle White Water Activity Center is a reference to the idiom, "being up shit creek without a paddle". Additionally, an advertisement near the business contains the words, "Head Up The Creek".

secrets.title: Albert Einstein
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: Artwork of Albert Einstein can be found on the wall of Vinewood Self Storage along Alta Street.

secrets.title: Bijan's Bugatti
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: The Truffade Adder that spawns on Portola Drive refers to the well-known Bijan's Bugatti Veyron commonly seen on Rodeo Drive in the exact same parking space.

secrets.title: Black Dahlia
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: Leonora Johnson's murder is a clear reference to the Black Dahlia murder: the victim, Elizabeth Short, was found murdered and severely mutilated on January 15, 1947 in Leimert Park, Los Angeles. Some of her wounds, like cuts on her breasts and portions of flesh removed, are similar to Leonora's. The murder was also referenced in L.A. Noire.

secrets.title: Black Panthers
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: A book inside Franklin's mansion is titled "The Black Punthers", referencing the Black Panthers.

secrets.title: Carson Palmer
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: In Franklin's house, there is a baseball jersey which has the number 3 with the surname "Palmer". This may very well be a reference to former NFL quarterback Carson Palmer, who wore number 3 for the Oakland Raiders and Arizona Cardinals.

secrets.title: Celebrity Mural
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: At Vinewood Wax Haven, there is a large mural featuring the heads of John Wayne, James Dean, Marilyn Monroe, and Charlie Chaplin.

secrets.title: Chris Edwards
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: A bench dedicated to the memory of late Rockstar Leeds artist Chris Edwards was placed in the Hill Valley Church graveyard in the next-gen release of GTA V.

secrets.title: Constellis/The Illuminati/Bohemian Grove
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: The private military company Merryweather Security is based off of Constellis, formerly known as Blackwater, Xe Services, and Academi, which is infamously responsible for several alleged human rights violations during the Second Gulf War. Both companies changed their names due to negative reputation, and Merryweather's logo is similar in styling to Constellis' former Blackwater logo. Furthermore, Merryweather's...

secrets.title: Cults
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: The Epsilon Program heavily parodies the Scientology cult. The Altruist Cult's website is based on that of the former cult, Heaven's Gate. Furthermore, a Morse code message on the site translates to "THE INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION HAS BEEN A DISASTER TO THE STABILITY OF THE HUMAN RACE", which is almost identical to the opening line of Industrial Society and Its Future, an essay written by the Unabomber, Ted Kaczynski.

secrets.title: Greyfriars Bobby
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: Sometimes, a dog can be seen walking into the Hill Valley Church cemetery. It will eventually stop in front of a headstone with a bouquet of flowers laid next to it. This is a reference to Greyfriars Bobby, a Skye Terrier from 19th century Edinburgh that spent 14 years guarding his master's grave, until he died in 1872.

secrets.title: Duke of Wellington Statue
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: The chicken statue located in front of Clucking Bell Farms has a traffic cone on top of it. This is possibly a reference to the Equestrian statue of the Duke of Wellington in Glasgow, as it has become a tradition to place a traffic cone on top of its head.

secrets.title: Frank Gusenberg
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: The Gusenberg Sweeper is named after hitman Frank Gusenberg who was shot and killed by a Thompson submachine gun in the Valentine's Day Massacre.

secrets.title: Giorgio Del Vecchio
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: The name of Del Vecchio Liquor is possibly a reference to the famous Italian Law philosopher, Giorgio Del Vecchio.

secrets.title: Hurricane Sandy
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: A hurricane flooding Liberty City is mentioned on Weazel News, Radio Mirror Park, Bless Your Heart, and Michael's TV during the mission Mr. Philips, referencing Hurricane Sandy, which devastated parts of New York City and New Jersey.

secrets.title: Iranian Revolution/Collapse of Communism
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: In By the Book, Michael De Santa claims that both the 1979 Iranian Revolution and the collapse of communism are reasons for why Chumash has many ethnically eastern residents.

secrets.title: J. Edgar Hoover
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: After Steve Haines' death in The Third Way, a news article will state that he was not married and lived with his mother, referencing the real-life FBI director J. Edgar Hoover.

secrets.title: Jesco White
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: On the north shore of the Alamo Sea, north of the westernmost dock is a run down house with a soapboxer tapdancing outside, while a woman sits nearby and watches on. The tapdancer is meant to be Jesco White from the documentary The Wild and Wonderful Whites of West Virginia.

secrets.title: Jesus Christ
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: Jesse is a soapboxer who can be found on Del Perro Pier, resembling a common depiction of Jesus Christ. He can be heard speaking various biblical phrases and often mentions his father, alluding to God. If killed in any way, one of his eyes will become swollen shut, while the other will be slightly open, resembling Jesus' face while crucified on the cross.

secrets.title: JFK Assassination Conspiracy
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: In a Weazel News article, IAA spokesperson Lucinda Jacob more or less jokingly states, "presidents that have tried to stop the IAA from performing our duty in ways we see fit have tended to wind up having their heads blown off". This is likely referencing the common conspiracy theory that the CIA - the IAA's real life counterpart - assassinated President John F. Kennedy.

secrets.title: Jim Cramer/Glenn Beck
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: The appearance of a soapboxer found in Paleto Bay, Bill Binder, is based on television personality Jim Cramer. Furthermore, his tactics of fear-mongering a potential economic apocalypse to obtain investors are based on Glenn Beck and Goldline.

secrets.title: Lindsay Lohan
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
secrets.summary: The characters Poppy Mitchell and Lacey Jonas possibly mock Lindsay Lohan. Lohan sued Rockstar Games in July 2014, alleging Jonas was based off of her likeness, though the lawsuit was ultimately thrown out in 2016, with a ruling on September 1 of that year stating: {{Quote|Even if we accept plaintiffs’ contentions that the video game depictions are close enough to be considered representations of the respective...

secrets.title: London Riots
secrets.area: References to Real Life People, Groups, and Events
